reason: Both are listed, SEC-regulated asset managers earning asset-based fees, so the business model matches. The products differ. Cohen & Steers sells specialized real-assets and alternative-income funds (mutual funds, ETFs, closed-end funds, separate accounts) globally to institutions and through advisors. Silvercrest is a US wealth manager that sells bundled wealth planning, family office services and an outsourced CIO (OCIO) service, mainly to high-net-worth families. Silvercrest also manages some long-only equity strategies for institutions and serves endowments and foundations. That is the only real overlap with Cohen & Steers' institutional clients. It is adjacent, not a direct competitor.
